root.claim: One deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes outputs $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$ for all $n$-bit inputs $x,y$ in worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, so the conjectured $n\log n$ lower bound fails in this model.
root.method: Reduce the product to normalized convolutions over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ computed by synthetic polynomial transforms, accelerate the transforms' address interchanges and butterfly layers by two recursive network procedures whose normalized cost grows by $s/W<m$ per level, assemble an exact multiplier, and sum the costs divided by the volume $V=\Theta(n)$.

motivation.text: A transform method that scans all $\Theta(n)$ stored bits once per level already pays $\Theta(n\log n)$ over $\Theta(\log n)$ levels, so going below $n\log n$ requires making both the data movement and the arithmetic of a level cheaper than a scan.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.claim: An eventual lower bound $T_A(n)\ge c_An\lg n$ for every fixed multiplication machine is refuted by one machine with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$, and a bound $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ even gives limit zero.

quote.quote: Its negation requires one machine satisfying $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$.

children.claim: Two disjoint contiguous $u$-bit address fields of a bit array of logical volume $V$, with arbitrary prefix, gap and suffix fields, can be interchanged by one fixed multitape procedure in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time for a fixed $\tau<1$, exactly for every payload.
children.method: Prove the bound for chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits preceded by a row field of length divisible by $W^k$, by running the bit network recursively; then supply rows from a few high digits, split a general width into base-$m$ power-width pieces, and pad binary ranges to powers of $q$.

motivation.text: Each edge of the network costs as many smaller interchanges as its matrix rank, and the ranks sum to less than wires times $m$, so a recursion on the chunk width saves a power of the width.

quote.quote: An edge matrix of rank $a$ will require $a$ smaller interchanges. Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: On an array of volume $V$ stored in lexicographic order, permuting or moving fixed radix-$q$ digit positions, splitting on one digit to apply a fixed pointwise map, and splitting whole rows cyclically into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$ each cost $O(V)$ on a fixed number of tapes.

quote.quote: Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

children.claim: If a target field $y\in[q^b]$ follows its control fields, the update $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\bmod q^b$ with an offset computable in $b^{O(1)}$ time, and multiplication of $y$ by a fixed rational unit, each cost $O(V)$, by splitting every fiber of $q^b$ blocks at the offset and merging the two pieces in swapped order.

quote.quote: costs $O(V)$ if the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time from the fixed number of control values.

children.claim: For $e=m^k$ and a row field preceding both chunks whose length is divisible by $W^k$, two chunks of $e$ radix-$q$ digits are interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time on fixed tapes, with a constant independent of all field lengths and of the data.
children.method: Split rows cyclically into $W$ role streams, run the bit network pointwise with address-shear frames so that its endpoint operator is the shear $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every row, implement each edge shear by smaller interchanges, convert the shear into an interchange by two linear updates, and solve the volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: Only the endpoint frames determine the result, so the intermediate frames can be chosen to make every edge's change of frame a low-rank shear, which is again an interchange problem of smaller width.

quote.quote: The intermediate frames are chosen so that every edge can be implemented by smaller calls to the same procedure.

children.claim: In the bit network on banks $X_a,Y_a$ indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$, triples of $[100]$, three stages of invocations send $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$, which over $\mathbb F_2$ exchanges the banks, and return every scratch wire to its arbitrary initial value.
children.method: In each invocation first subtract the scratch wires' current effect on the targets, then copy, gather, scatter and side-inject, then undo gather and copy, so the net change is $y\gets y+x$; compose a forward, an inverse and a forward stage, one per tensor coordinate.

motivation.text: When the network is run on arrays, its scratch roles are fed with existing data rows, so the exchange must be correct for arbitrary initial scratch values and must give them back unchanged.

quote.quote: The scalar network allows these role values to be arbitrary, so the split supplies its scratch roles from existing rows.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial side and central scratch vectors $a,c$, the eight-row schedule changes the targets by $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independent of $a,c$, and restores the scratch wires.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: In the bit construction the central path contributes $|S\cap T|\bmod2$ from $x_T$ to $y_S$, the side wires cancel exactly the pairs with $|S\cap T|=1$, and the self coefficient is one, so the net map is $y\gets y+x$.

quote.quote: In the bit case, the central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$.

children.claim: Forward, inverse and forward stages give $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y+x)\mapsto(-y,y+x)\mapsto(-y,x)$, each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

quote.quote: Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.salient: The net effect $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ does not depend on the arbitrary initial scratch values, and every scratch value comes back unchanged.

children.claim: If each wire carries an array stored at vertex $v$ as $D_v$ applied to its logical array, with one invertible frame $D_v$ shared by all wires at a gate and $D_vD_u^{-1}$ applied on each edge, then the network implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, so the route from role $w$ to $\rho(w)$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ whatever the intermediate frames.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: Labeling every gate and terminal of the bit network by a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F=(\mathbb Q^{h})^{\otimes3}$ and assigning projection matrices gives endpoint difference $I_m$ on every role and edge-rank sum $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$, whence $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$.
children.method: Attach nested labels built from tensor products of triple indicators, so every edge joins comparable labels and its matrix rank is the label-dimension change; telescope the signed changes at gates to the terminal total $W_{\rm b}m-2N$, add twice the losses on the only decreasing edges, and add the $N$ ranks of the negative source projections.

motivation.text: The ranks count the child calls, and the terminal labels force a total of about $W_{m b}m$; the saving can only come from keeping the dimension lost on decreasing edges small compared with $N$.

quote.quote: The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

children.claim: Under the form $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ on $\mathbb Q^h$, nondegenerate with eigenvalues $1$ and $-91/9$, triple indicators satisfy $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-|S||T|/9=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$, so every triple line is nondegenerate and triples meeting in exactly one point are orthogonal.

quote.quote: Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

children.claim: The terminal labels are $U_a=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$ to $\mathcal F$ on $X_a$, $0$ to $U_a^\perp$ on $Y_a$, and $0$ to $\mathcal F$ on scratch roles, so source dimensions sum to $N$ and sink dimensions to $W_{\rm b}m-N$, and since gate contributions cancel the signed changes sum to $W_{\rm b}m-2N$.

quote.quote: Thus the signed dimension changes will sum to $Wm-2N$, because the contributions at gates cancel.

children.claim: At stage $j$, with $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$, $P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$ and $B=P^\perp\subset A$, an $X$ wire's label grows from $A\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $(A\otimes F)\otimes Q$ and a $Y$ wire's from $B\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $(P\otimes\langle t\rangle)^\perp_{A\otimes F}\otimes Q$, and these are exactly the next stage's incoming labels and the terminal labels.

quote.quote: These transitions expose one tensor factor at each stage.

children.claim: Ordering the gates as $Y$-side, $Y$-center, $X$-side, $X$-center, $Y$-center, $Y$-side, $X$-center, $X$-side and labeling them inside $A\otimes F=(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes F)$, side wires pass through $P\otimes\langle t_X\rangle\subset P\otimes t_Y^\perp$, and the only decrease is each central wire's single return from $A\otimes F$ to $B\otimes F$.

quote.quote: The gate order below confines all decreases to this return, while the other edges realize the prescribed stage transitions.

children.claim: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels, the only decreasing edges are the $Ic$ central edges from time 3 to time 4, each losing dimension $h$, so $L=Ich$ and the absolute label changes sum to $W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L$.
children.method: Tabulate the orthogonal residual of every edge type by splitting $A=B\perp P$ and $F=\langle t\rangle\perp t^\perp$, check the inclusions that need the neighbor relation, and telescope the signed changes at the gates.

motivation.text: Each edge's cost will be the dimension of its residual, so an edge-by-edge table both proves that adjacent labels nest and turns the total into terminal data plus twice the losses.

children.claim: On a side wire joining neighboring triples, $(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes\langle t_X\rangle)\subset(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t_Y^\perp)$ because $t_X\perp t_Y$, with residual $P\otimes\langle t_X,t_Y\rangle^\perp$ of dimension $h-2$.

quote.quote: The side edge $2\to5$ uses the neighbor relation essentially.

children.claim: By the residual table, label dimension is nondecreasing on every edge except the central edge from time 3 to time 4, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$ of dimension $h$.

quote.quote: Label dimension is nondecreasing along every edge except center $3\to4$, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$.

children.claim: Every touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label, so the signed changes telescope to sink minus source dimensions, $W_{\rm b}m-2N$.

quote.quote: The signed sum of dimension changes telescopes at every gate: each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label.

children.claim: With $I=3v^2$ invocations and $c$ central wires each there are $Ic$ decreasing edges, each losing $h$, so replacing signed by absolute changes adds $2L$ with $L=Ich$.

quote.quote: There are $Ic$ decreasing edges, each of loss $h$; replacing signed changes by absolute changes adds $2L$.

children.claim: With $I=3v^2$ invocations, $c_{\rm b}=100$ central wires each, $h=100$ and $N=v^3$, $v=\binom{100}{3}$, the loss ratio is $L_{\rm b}/N=3\cdot100\cdot100/v=100/539<1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: With the projection $P_U$ along $U^\perp$ at each gate or sink with label $U$, $-P_{U_a}$ at the source of $X_a$ and $0$ at every other source, every role has endpoint difference $I_m$ and the edge ranks sum to $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$, a deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$ below $W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Use that $P_V-P_U$ for nested nondegenerate labels $U\subset V$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its complement, so its rank is the label change, and count separately the $N$ first edges on the $X_a$, where the negative source projection adds rank one.

motivation.text: Nested labels make each edge's change of frame count the smaller operations it needs, and the bit construction must add a source contribution so that every endpoint difference is exactly the identity.

quote.quote: Their dimension changes count the smaller operations needed on an edge, with an additional source contribution in the bit construction.

children.claim: For nested nondegenerate labels $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ has rank $\dim V-\dim U$, and reversing an edge only negates it.

quote.quote: Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

children.claim: The only exceptions are the $N$ first edges on the $X_a$: their first gate has label exactly $U_a$, so the edge matrix is $P_{U_a}-(-P_{U_a})=2P_{U_a}$, of rank one where the label change is zero, adding $N$ to $W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b}$.

quote.quote: Its first edge matrix is therefore $2P_{U_a}$, of rational rank one, where the corresponding dimension change was zero.

children.claim: Hence $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$, which falls short of $W_{\rm b}m$ by $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$ since $L_{\rm b}<N/2$.

quote.quote: Its deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

children.claim: On the route from $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other route runs from source matrix $0$ to sink label $\mathcal F$ with matrix $I_m$, so $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$ for every role $w$.

quote.quote: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.claim: The relative deficit $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$ exceeds $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and $\log m<20$ gives $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta_{\rm b})=s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

adds.name: bank size
adds.meaning: The number $v^3=\binom{100}{3}^3$ of entries $a\in\mathcal T^3$ in each of the two data banks.

adds.name: ground-set size
adds.meaning: The number of elements, 100, of the set whose three-element subsets index each bank coordinate.

adds.name: total label loss
adds.meaning: The total label dimension lost on the decreasing edges of the bit network.

adds.name: label space
adds.meaning: The $m$-dimensional space $(\mathbb Q^h)^{\otimes3}$ with the tensor bilinear form, whose nondegenerate subspaces label the vertices.

adds.name: triple indicator
adds.meaning: The 0/1 indicator vector in $\mathbb Q^h$ of a three-element subset $T$.

children.salient: Every role, scratch included, must end with the full shear $I_m$, yet the edges need strictly fewer than $W_{\rm b}m$ unit-rank operations: the deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}$ is positive because only $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539<1/2$ of the dimension is ever lost.

children.claim: For a fixed rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ and a fixed odd prime $q$ avoiding its factors' denominators, the address shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ takes exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit field pairs plus $O(V)$ further work.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower-triangular $E_1,E_2$ and a partial permutation $\Pi$ of rank $a$, apply the triangular factors as controlled shifts in tape order, and realize each one of $\Pi$ by one interchange between two controlled updates.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts are linear-time when the target follows its controls, which is exactly the direction of lower-triangular changes of coordinates, so only the rank-$a$ middle factor needs interchanges.

quote.quote: Lemma~\ref{lem:ordered-affine-streams} updates a later field using earlier fields in linear time. Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Elimination with the topmost nonzero row and its rightmost nonzero entry as pivot, using only lower-triangular row and column operations, gives $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with $\Pi$ having exactly $a$ ones.

quote.quote: Thus the final partial permutation matrix has exactly $a$ ones.

children.claim: Choosing $q$ to avoid every denominator and diagonal numerator in the finite table of factors, the factorization specializes to $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with invertible triangular factors.

quote.quote: All these rational identities then specialize to $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$, and the triangular factors remain invertible there.

children.claim: A lower-triangular change of $H$ or of $D$ updates its $m$ coordinates in descending physical order, each by a controlled shift from earlier fields, so it costs $O(V)$.

quote.quote: A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: A one of $\Pi$ at $(i,j)$ is done by $D_j\leftarrow D_j+H_i$, an interchange of $H_i$ and $D_j$, and $D_j\leftarrow H_i-D_j$, which turns $(h,d)$ into $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange, so the shear uses exactly $a$ interchanges.

quote.quote: On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$.

adds.name: matrix rank
adds.meaning: The rational rank of the shear matrix, equal to the number of interchanges the shear needs.

adds.name: partial permutation
adds.meaning: The 0/1 matrix with exactly $a$ ones, at most one per row and column, between the two triangular factors.

adds.name: digits per field
adds.meaning: The number of radix-$q$ digits in each of the $2m$ fields of the two chunks.

children.claim: Splitting rows cyclically into $W$ role streams of identical shape and volume $V/W$, running each gate pointwise and applying the shear $\Phi_{A_e}$ on each edge, so that role arrays sit in frames $\Phi_{M_v}$, the physical output on role $\rho(w)$ is $\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$, and merging rows back yields $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every row, scratch rows included.

quote.quote: The result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The updates $D\leftarrow D-H$, $H\leftarrow H+D$, $D\leftarrow H-D$ send $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$; the outer two are linear-cost controlled updates of the later group, so only the middle shear uses the network.

quote.quote: The transformation sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$.

children.claim: If $F_k$ bounds time divided by logical volume for width $e=m^k$, then $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, and $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.
children.method: Count the child calls (one per unit of edge rank, $s$ in all, each on a stream of volume $V/W$), charge splitting, gates, triangular updates and the fixed-tape schedule to $O(V)$ at the node, and sum the resulting geometric series.

motivation.text: Dividing cost by volume, each level multiplies the recursive cost by $s/W$ while the parameter grows by $m$; because $s/W<m$, this ratio is a power $m^	au$ with $	au<1$, which is the whole saving.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

children.claim: The child calls number exactly $s=\sum_e\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}A_e$, since the shear lemma uses one interchange per unit of rank, and each acts on one role stream of volume $V/W$ with all other fields as spectators.

quote.quote: The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly $s$. Each acts on one role stream of volume $V/W$, retaining all other fields as spectators.

children.claim: Splitting, merging, gates and triangular updates are fixed in number and cost $O(V)$, and width $k=0$ is a single-digit interchange, so $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.

quote.quote: Splitting, merging, gates, and triangular operations have total cost $O(V)$ because their number is fixed.

children.claim: With $s/W<m^\tau$, the sum $\sum_{j=0}^k(s/W)^j$ is at most $k+1=O(m^{k\tau})$ when $s/W\le1$ and $O((s/W)^k)$ otherwise, so $F_k=O(m^{k\tau})=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: For $a=s/W<m^\tau$ the geometric sum $\sum_{j=0}^k a^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$.

children.claim: Parking the $W-1$ inactive role streams on a stack and reusing the same tapes at every depth costs $O(V)$ per node because $s$ is fixed, so temporary storage does not enter the factor $s/W$.

quote.quote: Temporary storage is therefore not substituted for logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

adds.name: normalized cost
adds.meaning: An upper bound on running time divided by logical volume for chunks of width $m^k$.

children.salient: Multiplying the width by $m$ multiplies the normalized cost by only $s/W<m^\tau$: the strict inequality $s<Wm$ alone becomes the power saving $e^\tau$ with $\tau<1$.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number of radix-$q$ digits in each of the two chunks, a power $m^k$ of $m$.

adds.name: recursion level
adds.meaning: The exponent with $e=m^k$, which is the depth of the recursion.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $10^6$ of the label space, which is also the number of fields each chunk is split into.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires (roles) of the bit network, among which the rows are split.

adds.name: edge-rank sum
adds.meaning: The total rational rank of the network's edge matrices, which is the number of child interchanges per call.

adds.name: first chunk vector
adds.meaning: The first chunk viewed as a vector of $m$ fields over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$.

adds.name: second chunk vector
adds.meaning: The second chunk viewed as a vector of $m$ fields over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$.

children.claim: For an arbitrary width $u$, rows supplied by the top $\rho=O(\log e)$ digits of both chunks and a base-$m$ split of the remaining width into power-width pieces give the interchange in $O(Vu^\tau)$, including padding of the binary ranges to $[q^e]$.
children.method: Exchange and join the high digits into a row field of range $q^{2\rho}\ge W^k$, pad the rows to a multiple of $W^k$, interchange the remaining $e-\rho=\sum_ja_jm^j$ digits as $a_j$ pieces of width $m^j$ by the power-width procedure, then separate the high digits and remove the padding.

motivation.text: The power-width procedure needs enough rows; a few high digits of the chunks themselves provide them, and moving those digits one at a time costs less than the target bound.

quote.quote: Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits. Their movement will cost less than the final bound.

children.claim: Exchanging and joining the top $\rho=\lceil k\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$ digits costs $O(V\rho)$ and yields a row field of range $q^{2\rho}\ge W^k$; padding it to a multiple of $W^k$ less than doubles the volume.

quote.quote: Exchanging and joining the high parts costs $O(V\rho)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}.

children.claim: Since each $a_j<m$ and $m^k<me$, the power-width calls cost $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$, and padded zero rows stay zero at completed calls.

quote.quote: The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: Padding each binary range $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ with $q^e\ge2^u$ raises the volume by less than $q^2$ and preserves entry order, and $e=O(u)$, so the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

adds.name: field width
adds.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two address fields being interchanged.

adds.name: prime radix
adds.meaning: A fixed odd prime used as the radix of the address digits, so that the network's rational matrices make sense modulo powers of $q$.

children.salient: The result is an exact permutation of addresses, yet it is computed through XOR combinations of intermediate data and costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, below the $O(Vu)$ of moving the $u$ bits one at a time.

children.claim: On an array of volume $V$ whose records are polynomials with $r$ complex fixed-point coefficients and whose address has $D\le d$ consecutive $K$-bit chunks, applying $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ to one common bit position of every chunk, followed by one truncation $Q_p$, costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed $\lambda'<1$ and errs by less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.
children.method: Write $H_0^{\otimes D}$ through $C^{\otimes D}$ for the kernel $C=H\mathsf SH$, compute $C^{\otimes e}$ by running the complex network on row-role streams with phase frames whose edges are $s_{\rm c}$ smaller $C$-layers separated by binary changes of basis, perform those basis changes by packed selected-bit additions, and evaluate the whole layer exactly with $o(p)$ guard bits before a single truncation.

motivation.text: Applying the $D$ butterfly factors one at a time costs $D$ passes over the whole array; the complex network lets the same rank-saving recursion as for interchange act on butterflies, at a cost sublinear in $D$.

quote.quote: We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.claim: For the complex network with binary labels and phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod4$, each edge change is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse per vector of an orthonormal residual basis, $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$ kernels in all, and after diagonal corrections every role receives $C^{\otimes m}$.
children.method: Use the Hamming weight modulo four of the projected address as a phase, split each edge's phase change along an orthonormal residual basis, turn each resulting character into a translation kernel by Hadamard conjugation, and telescope the frames along routes, correcting the 27 inverted coordinates with $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

motivation.text: Frames that are all diagonalized by $H^{\otimes m}$ make every edge a product of two-point kernels of the same kind as the target, while the endpoint $C^{\otimes m}$ differs from the normalized butterfly layer only by phases and a scale.

quote.quote: For the numerical procedure, the endpoint operator becomes the simultaneous $H_0$ layer after diagonal phase operations and a dyadic scale.

children.claim: Over $\mathbb F_2$ every nonzero edge residual is nondegenerate and contains a norm-one vector, hence is nonalternating and has an orthonormal basis.

quote.quote: Thus every nonzero residual is nonalternating.

children.claim: Since $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)=\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)-2|\operatorname{supp}(z)\cap\operatorname{supp}(w)|$, weight is additive modulo four on orthogonal binary vectors, so for $V=U\perp E$ with orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $E$, $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]\bmod4$.

quote.quote: If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is additive modulo four.

children.claim: Each $v\in\mathcal B$ has odd weight, so its phase is $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}=\frac{1+i^\varepsilon}2+\frac{1-i^\varepsilon}2(-1)^{v\cdot x}$, and conjugation by $H^{\otimes m}$ turns $(-1)^{v\cdot x}$ into the translation $X_v$, giving $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

quote.quote: The displayed phase therefore becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.
